detail:
MedlinePlus' medical encyclopedia describes Long COVID symptoms that may last for weeks, months, or longer and notes that while many people have mild symptoms, Long COVID can be disabling for some. Because it is not one single condition, management is not one single treatment: clinicians address the problems each person actually has, such as breathing difficulty, cognitive symptoms, sleep problems, mood symptoms, or autonomic symptoms, and treat identifiable conditions that follow infection.

One widely reported feature, post-exertional malaise, means symptoms worsen after physical or mental exertion; it changes how rehabilitation and activity are paced, favoring gradual, symptom-guided plans over pushing through crashes. Ongoing follow-up matters because new symptoms can also signal a different condition that needs its own workup.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about a follow-up plan for persistent symptoms.
summary: MedlinePlus notes that Long COVID has no single proven treatment, so care is organized around the specific symptoms and conditions a person has, with follow-up to track recovery and to check for other causes.
takeaways: care is organized around your specific symptoms
symptoms often improve slowly over time
post-exertional worsening changes how activity is paced
keep follow-up appointments; new symptoms need evaluation
title: Managing Long COVID: symptom-by-symptom care
